passages.note: His own newsletter opposes SEA 285's criminal camping ban and criticizes fines, but names no penalty rule of his own, so it does not separate rungs 1, 2 and 3 (his described amendment is his account of an act, not a record).
Forum answers cover housing affordability and other topics but say nothing about penalties for sleeping or camping in public.
News excerpt about the forum; nothing on public sleeping or camping.

rows.reasoning: In his newsletter Pierce opposes SEA 285, saying "Criminalizing street camping and sleeping does nothing to solve the root causes of homelessness" and that "fines will continue the cycle of poverty", which places him against "Banning public camping and sleeping with criminal penalties". He does not state that there should be "no penalties of any kind", that public sleeping should simply be decriminalized, or that enforcement should hinge on available shelter beds with citations diverted to services, so the rungs on that side are not separated.

quotes.text: Criminalizing street camping and sleeping does nothing to solve the root causes of homelessness. In fact, a criminal record will add additional barriers to recovery and fines will continue the cycle of poverty.

I offered an amendment to this bill that would have prevented it from becoming effective until residential treatment facilities are operating that have the capacity to provide substance use disorder and mental health treatment to all of Indiana’s unhoused who need it.
